qs.q: Stress occurs:
o: With inexperienced pilots when the situational demands exceed their individual capabilities.
While monitoring the progress of motor programmes.
While concentrating on routine procedures.

qs.q: Divided attention is the ability:
o: To overcome mental blocks.
To execute several mental activities at almost at the same time.
To train or practice regularly.

qs.q: Stress promotes:
o: A decrease in physical strength rather than promoting mental performance.
An increase in physical strength rather than promoting mental performance.
An increase in mental performance rather than promoting physical strength.

qs.q: An over stressed pilot may show the following symptoms:
o: Deterioration in motor coordination.
Concentration and determination to complete the task.
Low pitch voice and slow speaking.

qs.q: Which of the following statement is correct?
o: Domestic stress will not affect the pilot's performance.
A moderate level of stress may improve performance.
A student will learn faster and better under severe stress.

qs.q: In the initial phase of flight training:
o: The pilot is competent to fly and knows at this stage what he can and cannot do.
The pilot is confident of his abilities and is able to negotiate all challenges in adverse situations.
The pilot is competent enough to fly the aircraft at this stage, but does not have a great deal of confidence in his/her abilities.

qs.q: A pilot is skilled when he:
o: Is familiar with his aircraft systems.
Trains or practices regularly, knows how to manage himself/herself and knows how to keep resources in reserve for coping with the unexpected.
Is directing and focusing psychological resources to enhance perception, performance and mental experience.

qs.q: Anthropometry is the study of:
o: Human workspace.
Human working conditions.
Human measurement.

qs.q: The human information processing system is highly efficient compared to computers because of its
o: Flexibility.
Working memory capacity.
Speed.

qs.q: Cockpit lights should:
o: Avoid harsh shadows and reflected glare.
Contain red filters.
Be covered with non-reflective plastic.

qs.q: Normally the design of aircraft uses measurements taken from:
o: The entire population disregarding both the 5% lowest and the 5% highest.
The entire population disregarding the 5% lowest.
The entire population.

qs.q: The most important requirement in the design of both displays and controls is:
o: Accessibility.
Positioning.
Standardization.

qs.q: Many pilots think ahead to deal with abnormal situations:
o: This has to be positively appreciated for it increases consistency in action.
This has to be rejected because the company draws the rules and the procedures they have to comply with.
This is dangerous for every situation is different.

qs.q: In an abnormal situation the pilot has an apparently correct explanation for the problem. The chance that he/she now ignores or devalues other relevant information, not fitting into his/her mental picture is:
o: The same, no matter if he/she has already made up his/her mind.
Decreasing.
Increasing.
qs.ex: Once a mental picture forms, confirmation bias grows: information that does not fit is more likely to be ignored.

qs.q: What are the main factors which bring about hypo vigilance are:
o: State of low fatigue is liable to cause phases of drowsiness and hypo-vigilance.
The monotony of the task, tiredness, the need for sleep and a lack of stimulation.
Stress, panic and the need to keep awake.

qs.q: Hypo vigilance is:
o: An extremely agitated state of panic or near panic.
A state of high fatigue liable to cause phases of drowsiness and hypo-vigilance.
Tends to lead to slower but more accurate responses.

qs.q: The human brain has:
o: Different reservoirs of resources for information-gathering, information- processing or action phase.
One reservoir of resources for the information-gathering, information- processing or action phase.
Different reservoir of resources for all phases of information stored briefly in our sensory memory.

qs.q: If a pilot has to perform two tasks requiring the allocation of cognitive resources:
o: The sharing of resources causes performance on each task to be reduced.
Resources are not limited, there is no deterioration in tasks being performed.
Multi-tasking is very common in aviation, hence pilots need not worry.

qs.q: What are the main signs indicating the loss of vigilance?
o: Increase in sensory perception and loss of concentration.
Decrease in sensory perception and sensation of muscular heaviness.
Blurred vision.

qs.q: Which are the preferred solutions to manage phases of reduced or low vigilance (hypovigilance)?
o: Healthy living and organizing periods of rest during the flight.
Exercise and meditation.
Selective attention to important matters only.

qs.q: The three distinct phases to developing a Motor Programme or skill (Anderson model) are:
o: Cognitive, associative and autonomous.
Training, practice and specialization.
Learning, perfecting and demonstrating.

qs.q: "Divided attention" is:
o: To execute several mental activities at almost the same time.
To prioritize the activities depending upon the relevance.
To develop skills to monitor multiple instruments.

qs.q: The available cognitive resources of the human brain:
o: Are of unlimited capacity of the central decision maker and working memory.
Are limited and make it impossible to perform two attentional tasks at the same time.
Can be trained to perform several attentional tasks together through motor programs.
qs.ex: Attention can only deal with one item at a time; resources are limited.

qs.q: The "cocktail party effect" is:
o: To exceed alcohol limits unintentionally.
The ability to pick up relevant information unintentionally.
To gather irrelevant information intentionally.

qs.q: Attention and Concentration is essential for pilots, however:
o: Capacity of attention and concentration is limited.
Sensory information is a stumbling block.
Attention cannot move very quickly from item to item.

qs.q: The first stage in the information process is:
o: Sensory stimulation.
Attention.
Perception.

qs.q: In short-term memory, information is stored for approximately ___ and its capacity is ___ items.
o: 40 to 60 seconds, 11 ± 3
20 to 30 seconds, 7 ± 2
10 to 20 seconds, 7 ± 2

qs.q: Motor programmes are:
o: Routines stored in sensory memory to be executed without continuous conscious control.
Held within the Long Term Memory and can be carried out without conscious thought.
Held within the Short Term Memory and can be carried out without conscious thought.

qs.q: NREM sleep Stage 4 is:
o: Beginning of deep sleep.
End of deep sleep.
Deep sleep.

qs.q: Concerning the capacity of the human long-term memory:
o: It's storage capacity is unlimited, although frequently there may be retrieval problems.
It's storage capacity is unlimited, there are no retrieval problems.
It's storage capacity is limited. Can be improved considerably by rehearsals.

qs.q: Murphy's law states:
o: If equipment is designed in such a way that it can be operated wrongly, then sooner or later, it will be.
Safety is paramount in designing any equipment.
Operational well-being of personnel is the industry need.

qs.q: Which of the following are primary sources of motivation?
o: Loyalty to the employer and high arousal level.
Skill learning, mnemonics and insight.
Satisfaction and feelings of achievement, rewards, punishment, and goal obtainment.

qs.q: Flying a coordinated turn is:
o: Skill-based behavior.
Attention-based behavior.
Experience-based behavior.

qs.q: The following factors can interfere with accurate situational awareness:
o: Stress, Boredom and Fatigue.
Emotional disturbance, Poor communication and Interruptions.
Both A and B are correct.

qs.q: Which of the following provides the basis of all perceptions?
o: We perceive most of the information reaching our senses at any moment.
Perception involves the conversion of the sensory information received into a meaningful structure.
Sensory information that we expect to receive is not easily perceived.

qs.q: How can optimum arousal and vigilance affect a pilot?
o: High arousal and vigilance are necessary for a pilot in all stages of flight.
In low arousal and vigilance, there is a real danger of attention becoming narrowed.
Too little arousal and vigilance have an inert affect, while too much has a hyper affect.

qs.q: An attention mechanism is required because:
o: Attention can move very quickly from item to item.
Attention is the deliberate devotion of the cognitive resources to a specific item.
There is a limit to the number of items held or maintained in short term memory (or working memory) and our channel capacity is limited.

qs.q: Hyper vigilance is:
o: Necessary in critical stages of a flight.
Necessary to allow flight crew to concentrate on instruments while landing.
In its most acute forms, an extremely agitated state of panic or near panic.

qs.q: What is meant by Episodic memory?
o: Memory of events or 'episodes' in our life, held in the long term memory.
Memory of events or 'episodes' in our life, held in the short term memory.
stores knowledge of the major events or episodes in the world in long term memory.

qs.q: Automated assistance for the human operator must be highly reliable, it :
o: Enables pilots to use their motor skills effectively in case the machine fails.
Induces hyper vigilance resulting in complacency.
Induces complacency, human expertise may gradually be lost if the machine fails.

qs.q: The achievable rate of human error after practice is:
o: 1 in 10 times.
1 in 100 times.
1 in 1000 times.

qs.q: Sleep is basically divided into two components.
o: Sleep credit and sleep debit.
Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep and Non-Rapid Eye Movement (NREM) sleep.
Light sleep and deep sleep.

qs.q: In the absence of all time cues (Free running circadian rhythms), the biological clock has a natural cycle of about:
o: 26 hours.
25 hours.
24 hours.

qs.q: Circadian cycles cause body temperature to change. At approximately what time of day is our temperature at its lowest value?
Flying from Hyderabad to Berlin with a layover of 22 hours, which time is relevant for your circadian rhythm?
o: ZT (zone time)
IST (Indian Standard Time)
LT (local time)
qs.ex: A layover under 24 h is too short to adapt: stay on home time.

qs.q: Performance loss may be present up to :
o: 60 minutes after awaking from a short sleep (nap).
30 minutes after awaking from a short sleep (nap).
20 minutes after awaking from a short sleep (nap).

qs.q: As a result of automation in cockpits,
o: Pilots may be replaced in the cockpit with Al in the near future.
Pilots, computers and machines are not alternatives, but complementary factors in ensuring flight safety.
Humans being responsible for the majority of accidents are dispensable.

qs.q: A skilled motor task will be momentarily disrupted by a startle reflex but return to normal within:
o: Five to ten minutes.
Five to ten seconds.
Two to three minutes.

qs.q: Easily observable indications of stress are:
o: perspiration, flushed skin, dilated pupils and slow breathing.
perspiration, flushed skin, low blood pressure and slow breathing.
perspiration, flushed skin, dilated pupils and fast breathing.

qs.q: The key to reducing cockpit workload is:
o: Good cockpit housekeeping.
Good communication and flying skills.
Thorough flight planning.

qs.q: Which of the following statement is correct with respect to REM sleep?
o: It is not important for the regeneration of mental and physical functions compared to all the other sleep stages.
The eye moves rapidly from side to side and the brain wave form is similar to that when a person is awake.
There is no eye movement and muscle activity.

qs.q: About ___ of a normal sleep is spent in Stage 2 sleep.
o: 30 percent.
75 percent.
50 percent.

qs.q: Fatigue is a:
o: Very deep tiredness due to the cumulative effects of a stressful lifestyle and/or living and working environment.
Very deep depression due to the cumulative effects of a low arousal and/or living and working environment.
Lethargic instant response of a person to the event or circumstances to which he is exposed.

qs.q: To avoid stress,
o: Wish it away, stress is not a natural part of life, hence avoidable.
Raise your vigilance and arousal to a high level to counter stress.
Know your limits and fly well inside them.

qs.q: Stress factors are cumulative. A cumulative score indicating that a person is life stress free is less than:
What does stress management involve?
o: Recognizing stress, accepting it and developing a coping strategy.
The recognition and removal of stress.
A constant stress prevention.

qs.q: What are the main effects of a lack of sleep loss on performance?
o: The brain activity, eye movement become faster and the cardiac activity increases.
It affects fatigue, concentration, attention, the risk of sensory illusions and mood disorders.
The physiological rhythms of a pilot in a new time zone will re-synchronize quickly to cater for sleep loss.

qs.q: In order to minimize the effects of crossing more than 3-4 zones with a layover more than 24 hours, it is advisable to:
o: Keep in swing with the rhythm of the arrival country for as long as possible and maintain regular living patterns.
Keep in swing with the rhythm of the departure country for as long as possible and maintain regular living patterns.
Keep in swing with the rhythm of the arrival country for as long as possible and maintain the living patterns of the departure country.
qs.ex: The book's advice for more than 3–4 zones with a layover over 24 h.

qs.q: Of the following statements concerning the effects of circadian rhythms on performance:
o: Sensorimotor performance is better in the morning whereas intellectual performance is better in the evening.
Sensorimotor and intellectual performance are better in the morning after a good night sleep.
Sensorimotor performance is better in the evening whereas intellectual performance is better in the morning.

qs.q: Melatonin secretion regulates:
o: Metabolism.
Sleep.
Muscles.

qs.q: The physiological rhythms of a pilot in a new time zone will resynchronize to this new time zone at a rate of about:
o: 1 - 1.5 hours a day.
2 - 2.5 hours a day.
3 - 3.5 hours a day.

qs.q: The readjustment of the biological rhythms after a time shift is normally more difficult with flights towards the:
o: West.
North.
East.
qs.ex: Eastbound takes about 1.5 days per zone, westbound about 1.

qs.q: The main functions of deep sleep are?
o: It essentially allows for motor programme reactivation and the reconstitution of mental agility.
It essentially allows for physical recovery and the reconstitution of neuron energy reserves.
It essentially allows for fatigue recovery and the reconstitution of the circadian cycle.

qs.q: Preventive efforts for mental disorders should be aimed at more common mental health problems such as:
o: Psychosis.
Depression, anxiety, and substance misuse.
Personal and financial issues.
